registros.prompt: Create an original pixel-art game sprite atlas for ONE natural resource: a dark coal seam deposit (coal), for a1930s Brazilian sertao RTS. Use the attached author-owned coal sprite only for identity/material, not its old lighting. Transparent background. A wide3-column by1-row atlas, precisely three equal square cells, each object independent, no text/grid/ground. Left: intact low irregular coal-bearing rocky outcrop, dark charcoal angular strata. Middle: same geological deposit after partial extraction, visibly lower with fewer upper pieces and newly exposed facets. Right: almost depleted, a very low fragment of the same deposit remaining near the ground. These are three NATIVELY DRAWN volumes, not scaled copies. Keep same logical footprint and bottom center alignment in all three cells. Target64x64px per derived sprite, legible at32x32px: crisp authored pixel art, 3-4 material values, no smooth plastic gradient. Light ONLY from above and slightly SOUTH/camera: the lower/front visible facets are illuminated cool medium-grey charcoal and rear/upper facets are darker black-grey midtone. In EACH cell the visible lower half must be clearly brighter than the upper half, roughly15-25 luma levels, while deep dark cracks remain thin. No east/west lighting bias. No bright white diamonds, no gold, no spheres, no cast-shadow disk, no floating cap, no grass or water. Preserve a natural angular rock seam identity, width similar in all states, upper ledges removed rather than whole sprite shrunk. Small palette with dark slate/charcoal and warm grey stone. Fully transparent clean alpha, no white or colored matte.

Edit this exact three-cell coal deposit atlas. Preserve all three silhouettes, black coal material, pixel art, cell spacing, grounded feet, decreasing height and width. ONLY repaint illumination natively: single overhead light slightly from SOUTH, bottom/front faces lighter medium charcoal grey and top/north faces distinctly darker. The average visible lower half of EACH deposit must be substantially brighter than its upper half; target lower surfaces about 20 luminance points lighter. No left/right lighting bias. Matte black coal with grey facets, no white highlights, no glow, no detached gravel, no cast shadow, transparent background. Three equal horizontal cells, same composition and three volume states. Do not change geometry.
